market_summary: The main event this week was the Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress in the US midterms. Traders took it as raising the odds of ending the Iran war, and Brent fell roughly 8-9% on Wednesday to a near two-month low. It was trading around $96-97 on Nov 5, well below the stale $107.03 Nov 3 mark. Hormuz risk has not gone away: the IRGC said two tankers and a tugboat caught fire on Nov 5 after allegedly using unauthorised routes. The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28, with two dissents in favour of a hike and markets pricing another hike. The US 10y is about 4.90% and the 2y about 4.59%. USD/JPY is near 158.4 with intervention worries, and the OAT-Bund spread is about 150bp after nearing 175bp on Oct 22 while the 2027 budget goes through the Assembly.

reasoning: Nothing clears the bar this week, and the account stays flat. (1) Oil: crude is pricing a binary outcome, a peace deal or continued attacks on Hormuz shipping. The Nov 3 marks are already $8-10 stale, so entry at the next official mark would come after a large, unknowable gap, and a stop tight enough to keep risk sensible would sit inside the daily noise. That leaves no edge in either direction (sources: tradingeconomics.com/commodity/crude-oil/news/598646; theglobeandmail.com/investing/article-oil-tumbles-as-investors-weigh-end-to-iran-war-after-us-democrats/; unitedagainstnucleariran.com/analysis/iran-shipping-update-november-5-2026). (2) US10Y: a lower oil price argues for a bond rally. Against that, the Fed has a hiking bias, with two dissents for a hike and a strong 55.5 ISM manufacturing reading. The 15bp fall in yields over the past week has already priced part of the oil move (sources: cnbc.com/2026/10/28/fed-interest-rate-decision-october-2026.html; seekingalpha.com/article/4958991). (3) JPY: there are arguments for a long. The US and Japan have intervened jointly before, and cheaper oil helps Japan's terms of trade. But MUFG notes persistent structural outflows and a weak link between rate gaps and the yen, and negative carry against a hiking Fed eats into any payoff. My honest probability is about 52%, which is not worth paying costs for (sources: tradingpedia.com/2026/11/04/yen-climbs-on-intervention-fears-softer-dollar/; tmgm.com MUFG yen note). (4) FR-DE: the spread could tighten further from 150bp or widen sharply again depending on the budget vote. I have no informational edge on that vote (source: pandaequityresearch.substack.com/p/the-spread-is-only-the-first-price). Finally, I used up my search budget before I could check the BoE decision, October payrolls, the BoJ and the ECB. Without those, I can't judge gilts, sterling, the euro, the Bund, the Swiss franc, the Aussie or the Canadian dollar. I will look again next week, once oil and the data have settled.
